day_shape: 69 items dominated by Khamenei funeral logistics and tributes across regime channels, UN Security Council session on Iran's attack on Bahrain with UK statement, CENTCOM claiming 14 Iranian drones downed, and IDF strike on Hezbollah operative in south Lebanon.

threads.label: Khamenei funeral preparations in Tehran
threads.summary: Iranian state media, Defa Press and Khamenei's office posted extensive logistics for Friday's farewell ceremony, with the Foreign Ministry spokesman claiming representatives from around 100 countries would attend. Tehran was divided into four traffic rings, 14 reception centres opened, and delegations including Lebanon's Supreme Shia Council and Nabih Berri's eulogy were announced.

threads.label: UNSC on Iran-Bahrain and CENTCOM posture
threads.summary: The UN Security Council convened at Bahrain's request following Iran's attack on the kingdom, with the UK's Ambassador Kariuki delivering a solidarity statement. CENTCOM Commander Adm. Brad Cooper said a joint C-UAS unit in Bahrain had shot down 14 Iranian one-way attack drones, while Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Bagheri denounced the Manama regional security dialogue.

threads.label: IDF operations in south Lebanon
threads.summary: The IDF said troops of the Egoz Commando Unit killed a Hezbollah operative emerging from a tunnel shaft at the Ali Taher ridge inside the south Lebanon security zone. Soldiers also located an underground shaft, rockets, mortars and explosive devices around At-Tiri and Maroun al-Ras.

threads.label: Iran internal security and Kurdish clashes
threads.summary: Defa Press claimed a five-man team from the dissolved Democrat group was dismantled on the north-west border, and reported three armed robbers killed in Zahedan. Iran International reported the re-arrest of environmental activists Houman Jokar and Sepideh Kashani, while the Jerusalem Post cited PJAK-IRGC clashes and further strikes on Kurdish opposition groups.

threads.label: Iran hardliner backlash over US MoU
threads.summary: Iran International reported ultra-hardliners accusing Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf and President Pezeshkian of a 'coup' over a US-Iran memorandum said to contradict the slain Supreme Leader's position. A separate report noted debate over dissolving the IRGC following the recent war.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz and Iran spy arrest
threads.summary: Khatam al-Anbiya Central Command warned any US interference in the Strait of Hormuz would meet a 'decisive and swift response'. Israeli authorities announced the arrest of Behrouz Sobirgon, a Tajik citizen with a Russian passport, on suspicion of spying for Iran since January 2026.

threads.label: Damascus explosion and Syria diplomacy
threads.summary: Syria's Ministry of Health reported five dead and 16 injured in an explosion at a café near the Damascus Palace of Justice, with the cause under investigation. The Jerusalem Post reported Syria's foreign minister visiting Beirut to meet government and Hezbollah leaders after Trump suggested Syria should 'take care of Hezbollah'.

events.title: Enabling Supersonic Overland Flight
events.summary: This proposal would advance the United States' leadership in next-generation aviation by replacing the longstanding prohibition on civil supersonic flight over land with a modern, performance-based regulatory framework. Consistent with national policy set forth by the Executive Order of June 6, 2025, Leading the World in Supersonic Flight, this action would enable the safe, efficient, and commercially viable operation of civil supersonic aircraft in the United States. Current regulations prohibit flight operations of civil aircraft at a true flight Mach number greater than 1 in the U.S., except under the conditions and limitations of an operation-specific authorization from the Administrator, to protect the public from sonic boom. FAA has determined the general ban on civil supersonic flight is outdated and no longer appropriate due to advancements in technology, flight techniques that prevent sonic booms from reaching the surface, and increased interest in civil supersonic flight. FAA proposes to repeal this outdated and unnecessary prohibition and establish a corresponding interim noise-based certification standard to allow supersonic flights without an operation-specific special authorization clearing the way for next-generation supersonic flight. This rule removes regulatory barriers, provides clear pathways for testing and early commercial operations, and positions the United States to serve as the leader in setting global standards for supersonic flight. These actions will ensure that the United States leads the world in the safe, lawful, and rapid development and deployment of next-generation supersonic aviation.
